Those who are guided by the Holy Spirit speak what is true with love and try to make peace with others ({{Galatians 5:22|Galatians 5:22}}; {{Ephesians 4:15|Ephesians 4:15}}; {{2 Timothy 2:23-26|2 Timothy 2:23}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{2 Timothy 2:23-26|26}}). 

- *Jealousy* (in Greek *zēlos*, meaning "zeal") can mean a positive "passionate commitment" or a negative "intense desire for others' things" (compare {{James 3:14-16|James 3:14}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{James 3:14-16|16}}). 

- *Rage* (violent and uncontrolled anger) is the opposite of self-control ({{Galatians 5:23|Galatians 5:23}}; see, for example, {{Acts 19:28|Acts 19:28}}; {{2 Corinthians 12:20|2 Corinthians 12:20}}; {{1 Timothy 3:3|1 Timothy 3:3}}; {{Titus 1:7|Titus 1:7}}). 

- *Rivalries* (or selfishness) oppose Christian love (compare {{Romans 2:8|Romans 2:8}}; {{Philippians 2:3|Philippians 2:3}}; {{James 3:14|James 3:14}}, {{James 3:16|16}}). 

- *Factions* (in Greek *haireseis*, meaning "heresies, factions, sects") refers to using different beliefs or practices to divide the community (compare {{1 Corinthians 11:17-19|1 Corinthians 11:17}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{1 Corinthians 11:17-19|19}}; {{2 Peter 2:1-3|2 Peter 2:1}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{2 Peter 2:1-3|3}}).

- *Drunkenness* does not belong in a Christian's life (see {{Luke 21:34|Luke 21:34}}; {{1 Corinthians 11:20-22|1 Corinthians 11:20}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{1 Corinthians 11:20-22|22}}; {{Ephesians 5:18|Ephesians 5:18}}). 

- *orgies*: Religious celebrations for false gods often included wild parties with lots of drinking and sexual sin (compare {{1 Peter 4:3|1 Peter 4:3}}). 

- *and the like*: This list shows examples of sinful behaviors (compare {{Mark 7:20-23|Mark 7:20}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{Mark 7:20-23|23}}; {{Romans 1:29-31|Romans 1:29}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{Romans 1:29-31|31}}; {{1 Corinthians 6:9-10|1 Corinthians 6:9}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{1 Corinthians 6:9-10|10}}; {{Ephesians 5:3-5|Ephesians 5:3}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{Ephesians 5:3-5|5}}; {{Colossians 3:5-8|Colossians 3:5}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{Colossians 3:5-8|8}}; {{1 Timothy 1:9-10|1 Timothy 1:9}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{1 Timothy 1:9-10|10}}; {{2 Timothy 3:2-5|2 Tim 3:2}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{2 Timothy 3:2-5|5}}; {{James 3:13-18|James 3:13}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{James 3:13-18|18}}; {{Revelation 21:8|Revelation 21:8}}). People living this way do not follow the Holy Spirit and so they do not show a relationship with God by faith. Such people will not inherit the kingdom of God. They remain slaves to their sinful nature ({{Galatians 4:8-9|Galatians 4:8}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{Galatians 4:8-9|9}}, {{Galatians 4:22-25|22}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{Galatians 4:22-25|25}}; compare {{Romans 6:16-22|Romans 6:16}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{Romans 6:16-22|22}}; {{1 Corinthians 6:9-10|1 Corinthians 6:9}}{{Romans 2:14-15|–}}{{1 Corinthians 6:9-10|10}}). They are not under God’s rule.

- Choosing to follow the Holy Spirit leads to a life that pleases God, unlike following sinful desires ({{Galatians 5:16|5:16}}; {{Galatians 5:19-21|5:19–21}}). Human effort and laws cannot achieve this (compare {{John 15:1-8|John 15:1}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{John 15:1-8|8}}). 

- This list of virtues addresses issues in the Galatian church. 

- *Love* is the greatest Christian virtue and includes all others ({{1 Corinthians 13:4-7|1 Corinthians 13:4}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{1 Corinthians 13:4-7|7}}). Only God's Spirit can help us love those who hate us (see {{Matthew 5:43-48|Matthew 5:43}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Matthew 5:43-48|48}}; {{Luke 6:35-36|Luke 6:35}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Luke 6:35-36|36}}). 

- *Joy* from the Holy Spirit does not depend on circumstances (see {{Romans 15:13|Romans 15:13}}; {{2 Corinthians 6:10|2 Corinthians 6:10}}; {{2 Corinthians 8:2|8:2}}; {{1 Thessalonians 1:6|1 Thessalonians 1:6}}). 

- *Peace* with God brings inner well-being ({{Romans 5:1|Romans 5:1}}; {{Ephesians 2:15|Ephesians 2:15}}; {{Philippians 4:6-7|Philippians 4:6}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Philippians 4:6-7|7}}; {{Colossians 1:20|Colossians 1:20}}). It helps us become peacemakers with others (see {{Matthew 5:9|Matthew 5:9}}; {{Romans 8:6|Romans 8:6}}; {{Romans 12:18|12:18}}; {{Romans 14:17-19|14:17}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Romans 14:17-19|19}}; {{2 Corinthians 13:11|2 Corinthians 13:11}}; {{Ephesians 4:3|Ephesians 4:3}}; {{Ephesians 6:15|6:15}}). 

- *Patience* (or tolerance or long-suffering) helps us endure difficult situations and be patient with others ({{Ephesians 4:2|Ephesians 4:2}}; {{2 Timothy 4:2|2 Timothy 4:2}}; {{James 5:10-11|James 5:10}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{James 5:10-11|11}}). God is patient with us ({{Exodus 34:6|Exodus 34:6}}; {{Psalm 103:8|Psalms 103:8}}; {{Romans 2:4|Romans 2:4}}; {{Romans 9:22|9:22}}; {{1 Timothy 1:16|1 Timothy 1:16}}; {{2 Peter 3:15|2 Peter 3:15}}). God promises to be with those who are patient with others ({{Isaiah 57:15|Isaiah 57:15}}). 

- *Kindness* means being generous and helping others, showing the same spirit of giving that God shows to us ({{Romans 2:4|Romans 2:4}}; {{Romans 11:22|11:22}}; {{Titus 3:4-6|Titus 3:4}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Titus 3:4-6|6}}). 

- *Goodness*: Compare {{Romans 15:14|Romans 15:14}}; {{Ephesians 5:9|Ephesians 5:9}}; {{2 Thessalonians 1:11|2 Thessalonians 1:11}}. 

- *Faithfulness* (or *faith*) means being reliable and trustworthy in our relationships, just as God is with us ({{1 Corinthians 1:9|1 Corinthians 1:9}}; {{1 Corinthians 10:13|10:13}}; {{2 Thessalonians 3:3|2 Thessalonians 3:3}}).

- Gentleness is the opposite of the bad behaviors in {{Galatians 5:20|5:20}} and requires strength (see {{Proverbs 15:1|Proverbs 15:1}}, {{Proverbs 15:4|4}}; {{Matthew 11:28-29|Matthew 11:28}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Matthew 11:28-29|29}}; {{Ephesians 4:2|Ephesians 4:2}}). 

- *Self-control*: The Holy Spirit does not allow immoral behavior but helps people avoid sin (compare {{Galatians 5:13|Galatians 5:13}}; {{Romans 6:14-18|Romans 6:14}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Romans 6:14-18|18}}; {{1 Thessalonians 4:3-7|1 Thessalonians 4:3}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{1 Thessalonians 4:3-7|7}}; {{1 Peter 2:16|1 Peter 2:16}}; see also {{Acts 24:25|Acts 24:25}}; {{Titus 1:8|Titus 1:8}}). 

- *Against such things there is no law*: Paul explains what is already obvious, that those led by the Holy Spirit do not need laws to guide them.

- People who trust in Jesus share in his death on the cross through faith (compare {{Galatians 2:19-20|2:19}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Galatians 2:19-20|20}}; {{Romans 6:1-23|Romans 6}}). They become new people ({{Romans 6:1-2|Romans 6:1}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Romans 6:1-2|2}}; {{2 Corinthians 5:17|2 Corinthians 5:17}}; {{Colossians 3:5-15|Colossians 3:5}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Colossians 3:5-15|15}}). They have left behind their sinful nature and the law (see {{Galatians 2:19|Galatians 2:19}}; {{Romans 7:4-6|Romans 7:4}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Romans 7:4-6|6}}; {{2 Corinthians 5:14|2 Corinthians 5:14}}; {{Colossians 3:1-4|Colossians 3:1}}{{Galatians 5:19-21|–}}{{Colossians 3:1-4|4}}). 

- *passions and desires*: Refer to {{Galatians 5:19-21|5:19–21}}.
Christians do not live by the law but instead let the Holy Spirit guide their lives.
The Galatian church seemed to struggle with divisions instead of following the guidance of the Holy Spirit (see also study note on 5:20; compare {{1 Corinthians 3:1-23|1 Corinthians 3}}).

- Some of the Galatians may have felt proud about how well they followed the law of Moses or how strong their faith was. However, truly godly people do not boast about what they have done. Instead, they humbly help others. 

- *watch yourself*: We can all be tempted to sin ({{Romans 3:9-20|Romans 3:9–20}}).
Paul explains how to lovingly help other Christians when they make mistakes.

Paul reminded the believers in Galatia to do good to one another. They needed to be humble and gentle. This was especially true when they corrected one another.

They needed to give freely to teachers who taught them the truth about Jesus. And they needed to help other believers with things that were hard for them. Paul described this as carrying one another’s heavy loads. It’s what Jesus taught people to do in Christ’s law.

At the same time, each Galatian believer was to carry their own load. This means that each believer is responsible to God for the choices they make. They can choose to act according to desires that are sinful. Or they can choose to act in ways that please the Holy Spirit.

Paul described these choices like seeds that people plant. What happens as a result of their actions is the crop that is harvested. When people follow Jesus’ example, the harvest is eternal life in God’s kingdom. But the harvest of sinful actions leads to death.

Living by the Spirit ({{Galatians 5:13-6:10|5:13–6:10}}) leads to doing good deeds ({{Galatians 6:1-5|6:1}}{{Galatians 5:13-6:10|–}}{{Galatians 6:1-5|5}}) and receiving blessings from the good work we do ({{Galatians 6:6-10|6:6}}{{Galatians 5:13-6:10|–}}{{Galatians 6:6-10|10}}).

Helping each other with problems ({{Galatians 6:1|6:1}}) follows Christ's command to love one another ({{Galatians 5:13-14|5:13}}{{Galatians 5:13-6:10|–}}{{Galatians 5:13-14|14}}; see also {{Leviticus 19:18|Leviticus 19:18}}; {{Matthew 22:36-40|Matthew 22:36}}{{Galatians 5:13-6:10|–}}{{Matthew 22:36-40|40}}; {{John 13:34|John 13:34}}; {{John 15:12|15:12}}; {{1 John 3:23|1 John 3:23}}).
People with a proud attitude wrongly think they are too important to help those who are weak (see study note on 6:1).

We should not think we are better than others. Instead, we should focus on our own actions and make sure we follow Christ in everything (see {{1 Corinthians 3:12-15|1 Corinthians 3:12}}{{Galatians 5:13-6:10|–}}{{1 Corinthians 3:12-15|15}}).
If believers take responsibility for themselves ({{Galatians 6:4|6:4}}), they will not treat others as if they are worth less than themselves ({{Galatians 6:3|6:3}}).

Supporting Christian teachers follows the guidance in {{Galatians 5:13|5:13}} and {{Galatians 6:2|6:2}} (see also {{1 Timothy 5:17-18|1 Timothy 5:17}}{{Galatians 5:13-6:10|–}}{{1 Timothy 5:17-18|18}}).
When Christians financially support those who teach God's message ({{Galatians 6:6|6:6}}), they gain spiritual benefits.

- *God is not to be mocked: *God cannot be deceived by people who only pretend to be spiritual. God knows what is truly in their hearts. Everyone will face the results of their actions.

- *Whatever a man sows*: see also {{Job 4:8|Job 4:8}}; {{Psalm 126:5|Psalms 126:5}}; {{Proverbs 22:8|Proverbs 22:8}}; {{Hosea 8:7|Hosea 8:7}}; {{Hosea 10:12-15|10:12}}{{Galatians 5:13-6:10|–}}{{Hosea 10:12-15|15}}; {{Luke 19:21-23|Luke 19:21}}{{Galatians 5:13-6:10|–}}{{Luke 19:21-23|23}}; {{1 Corinthians 3:12-15|1 Corinthians 3:12}}{{Galatians 5:13-6:10|–}}{{1 Corinthians 3:12-15|15}}; {{1 Corinthians 9:11|9:11}}; {{2 Corinthians 9:6|2 Corinthians 9:6}}.

Living to please the Spirit is only possible with the Spirit's power ({{Galatians 3:3|3:3}}; {{Galatians 5:16|5:16}}). People who rely on their own efforts or do whatever they want are in the same situation: They live to satisfy their own sinful desires. These people will face decay and death. Those who live by the Spirit's power and trust in God will gain everlasting life.

- *Let us not grow weary*: Avoid letting sinful behavior sneak in or relying on strict rules instead of following the Spirit ({{Galatians 5:25|5:25}}). 

- *for in due time we will reap a harvest*: This promise encourages Christians to keep doing good work (see {{Romans 8:28|Romans 8:28}}). 

- *if we do not give up*: God's promises to believers require them to keep their faith strong (see also {{Luke 18:1|Luke 18:1}}; {{2 Corinthians 4:1|2 Corinthians 4:1}}).

- *Therefore*: This statement forms an *inclusio* that marks the beginning and end of this section ({{Galatians 5:13-6:10|5:13–6:10}}), like two bookends that hold it together by repeating the theme from {{Galatians 5:13|5:13}}: Freedom in the Spirit urges us to do good to others with love. 

- Doing good to those in the faith community shows God's faithfulness to his children. This action directly shows how God meets all their needs.

Jews who believed that Jesus is the Messiah didn’t need to obey the Law of Moses. Yet Jewish leaders treated Jews badly if they didn’t obey Jewish laws.

Some Jewish believers in Galatia didn’t want to be treated badly for following Jesus. So they wanted everyone to think that they still followed all the Jewish laws.

They also tried to make Gentile believers follow Jewish laws about circumcision. Paul explained that the laws about circumcision didn’t matter anymore. What matters is the new creation that Jesus brought when he died on the cross.

Paul’s body had scars from being treated badly for following Jesus. He was willing to suffer for belonging to Jesus.
Paul picked up the writing tool from his *amanuensis* (secretary) and wrote a postscript himself. He did this to prove the letter was truly his and to make a final appeal.
Despite their theological arguments, the false teachers were self-serving. They wanted approval from non-Christian Jews and cared more about their reputation than honoring God.

- Unlike the false teachers mentioned in {{Galatians 6:12-13|6:12–13}}, Paul wanted to increase God's glory. He did not want to increase his own reputation. Boasting about following the law would take away from recognizing the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. 

- In the Greco-Roman world, the cross seemed foolish to non-believers ({{Galatians 5:11|5:11}}; {{1 Corinthians 1:23|1 Corinthians 1:23}}; compare {{John 6:53-61|John 6:53}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{John 6:53-61|61}}). But it is the foundation of a Christian's faith and hope ({{1 Corinthians 1:17-18|1 Corinthians 1:17}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{1 Corinthians 1:17-18|18}}; {{1 Corinthians 15:3|15:3}}; {{Philippians 2:8-11|Philippians 2:8}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Philippians 2:8-11|11}}; {{Colossians 1:20-22|Colossians 1:20}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Colossians 1:20-22|22}}; {{Colossians 2:14-15|2:14}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Colossians 2:14-15|15}}).

The Galatians misunderstood the good news about Jesus. A new creation comes through Jesus Christ by the Holy Spirit, not by human effort (compare {{2 Corinthians 5:16-17|2 Corinthians 5:16}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{2 Corinthians 5:16-17|17}}).

- *This rule* is trusting Jesus for salvation ({{Galatians 6:14-15|6:14}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Galatians 6:14-15|15}}). 

- *even to the Israel of God*: The Greek word *kai *is usually translated as "and." It can also mean "even." If it means "and," then the *Israel of God* is a different group from *all who walk by this rule.* If it means "even," then they are the same group. 

The Jewish people still have a special identity before God ({{Romans 9:1-5|Romans 9:1}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Romans 9:1-5|5}}; {{Romans 10:1-4|10:1}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Romans 10:1-4|4}}; {{Romans 11:1-32|11:1}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Romans 11:1-32|32}}). Gentiles (non-Jewish people) who believe have been included, and Jews who do not believe have been removed from spiritual Israel ({{Romans 11:17-24|Romans 11:17}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Romans 11:17-24|24}}; compare {{Philippians 3:2-3|Philippians 3:2}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Philippians 3:2-3|3}}; {{Colossians 2:11-12|Colossians 2:11}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Colossians 2:11-12|12}}). Paul sees all Christians as the true Israel (see {{Romans 2:28-29|Romans 2:28}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Romans 2:28-29|29}}; {{Romans 9:6-8|9:6}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Romans 9:6-8|8}}; compare {{Galatians 4:21-31|Galatians 4:21}}{{Galatians 6:12-13|–}}{{Galatians 4:21-31|31}}). 

The phrase *the Israel of God* is not found elsewhere in the New Testament or other writings. Perhaps false teachers promised this identity to Gentiles who accepted circumcision. If so, Paul shows why their argument was wrong: The non-Jewish Christians in Galatia did not need circumcision, as they were already God's *Israel—*his true people—through faith in Christ.

- *let no one cause me trouble*: No one has the right to criticize Paul or his message because he is a proven servant of Jesus. 

- Paul's scars (in Greek *stigmata*) likely came from the severe persecution he experienced as a servant of Jesus (see {{Acts 14:19|Acts 14:19}}; {{2 Corinthians 6:4-10|2 Corinthians 6:4–10}}; {{2 Corinthians 11:21-33|11:21–33}}). Unlike the physical mark of circumcision that false teachers in Galatia wanted to force on non-Jewish Christians, Paul's scars from suffering showed he was truly the servant of Jesus (compare {{Exodus 21:6|Exodus 21:6}}).

Paul prayed at the end of this letter just as he did at the start ({{Galatians 1:3-4|1:3–4}}). The Galatians needed the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ to be with their spirit more than they needed the law.
